sentences.en: I read a book about a philosopher.

english: to trade, to earn a living buying & selling, to deal in such-&-such a commodity
note: "Berdagang" is a formal/standard verb for trading or doing business; everyday speech often uses "jualan" instead; related words include "dagang" (trade/commerce) and "pedagang" (trader/merchant).

sentences.text: Ibu saya berdagang sayur di pasar.
sentences.en: My mother sells vegetables at the market.

sentences.text: Pak Wayan berdagang kain di Bali.
sentences.en: Mr. Wayan trades cloth in Bali.

sentences.text: Mereka berdagang setiap hari.
sentences.en: They trade every day.

english: to think, to ponder, to ruminate
note: "Berpikir" is a standard/formal verb for thinking; informal speech often uses "pikir" alone; related: "pikiran" (thought/mind), "memikirkan" (to think about something).

sentences.text: Dia berpikir sebelum menjawab pertanyaan itu.
sentences.en: He thinks before answering that question.

sentences.text: Saya berpikir tentang liburan ke Bali.
sentences.en: I am thinking about a holiday to Bali.

sentences.text: Anak itu berpikir dengan serius.
sentences.en: That child is thinking seriously.

english: a seed, seed, a berry, a pip beans (e.g. coffee beans), the stone (in stone fruit)
note: "Biji" is a general classifier for small round objects like seeds, beans, and pips; it also functions as a counter word (e.g., tiga biji = three pieces/seeds); not to be confused with "buah" which refers to fruit as a whole.

sentences.text: Saya menanam biji kopi di kebun.
sentences.en: I am planting coffee beans in the garden.

sentences.text: Adik memegang biji mangga yang besar.
sentences.en: My younger sibling is holding a big mango stone.

sentences.text: Ibu membeli biji cabai di pasar.
sentences.en: Mom bought chili seeds at the market.

note: 'Bola voli' is the standard Indonesian term for volleyball; 'bola' means ball and is used with other sports too (bola basket, bola sepak).

sentences.text: Kami bermain bola voli di pantai.
sentences.en: We play volleyball at the beach.

sentences.text: Saya suka menonton bola voli bersama teman.
sentences.en: I like watching volleyball with friends.

sentences.text: Bola voli itu warna putih dan biru.
sentences.en: That volleyball is white and blue.

note: 'Gitar' is a direct loanword from English/Dutch; commonly used in casual speech, related words include 'bermain gitar' (to play guitar) and 'gitaris' (guitarist).

sentences.text: Dia bermain gitar di pantai.
sentences.en: He plays guitar on the beach.

sentences.text: Saya ingin belajar main gitar.
sentences.en: I want to learn to play guitar.

sentences.text: Gitar ini milik kakak saya.
sentences.en: This guitar belongs to my older sibling.

english: special, exceptional, out of the ordinary
note: "Istimewa" is a neutral-to-formal adjective meaning special or exceptional; commonly used in everyday compliments, menus, and celebrations — similar to "spesial" but feels more naturally Indonesian.

sentences.text: Nasi goreng di sini sangat istimewa.
sentences.en: The fried rice here is very special.

sentences.text: Hari ini adalah hari yang istimewa.
sentences.en: Today is a special day.

sentences.text: Hadiah ini sangat istimewa untuk saya.
sentences.en: This gift is very special to me.

note: "Juta" means million; used in prices and large numbers; e.g. "satu juta" = one million (rupiah), often heard when shopping or discussing salaries.

sentences.text: Harga motor itu dua juta rupiah.
sentences.en: The price of that motorcycle is two million rupiah.

sentences.text: Dia punya satu juta rupiah di bank.
sentences.en: She has one million rupiah in the bank.

sentences.text: Tiket pesawat itu tiga juta rupiah.
sentences.en: That plane ticket is three million rupiah.

english: to lose (a contest/fight etc.), to be defeated
note: "Kalah" means to lose a game, race, or fight; opposite is "menang" (to win); commonly used in sports and games contexts.

sentences.text: Tim saya kalah dalam pertandingan sepak bola.
sentences.en: My team lost in the football match.

sentences.text: Adik saya kalah main kartu tadi.
sentences.en: My younger sibling lost playing cards just now.

sentences.text: Jangan sedih kalau kalah bermain.
sentences.en: Don't be sad if you lose playing.

english: less..., not quite..., don't/doesn't really..., isn't/aren't really...
note: "Kurang" before an adjective softens it, meaning 'not quite' or 'not very'; don't confuse with 'kurang' meaning 'minus' in math or 'less of something'.

sentences.text: Makanan ini kurang pedas untuk saya.
sentences.en: This food is not spicy enough for me.

sentences.text: Kamar itu kurang bersih.
sentences.en: That room is not very clean.

sentences.text: Saya kurang suka kopi pahit.
sentences.en: I don't really like bitter coffee.

english: a song, a tune, a piece of music
note: 'Lagu' is a neutral everyday word for a song or tune; 'musik' refers to music in general, while 'lagu' means a specific song or piece.

sentences.text: Saya suka lagu itu.
sentences.en: I like that song.

sentences.text: Dia menyanyi lagu yang indah.
sentences.en: She sings a beautiful song.

sentences.text: Lagu ini sangat populer di sini.
sentences.en: This song is very popular here.

english: to repair something, to fix something broken
note: "Memperbaiki" is the formal/full form; "perbaiki" is the informal imperative or base form — both mean to fix/repair something broken, commonly used for objects like phones, bikes, or appliances.

sentences.text: Ayah memperbaiki sepeda saya yang rusak.
sentences.en: Dad is fixing my broken bicycle.

sentences.text: Tolong perbaiki lampu di kamar ini.
sentences.en: Please fix the light in this room.

sentences.text: Dia memperbaiki hp-nya sendiri.
sentences.en: She is fixing her own phone.

note: 'Menang' means 'to win' or 'winning'; the opposite is 'kalah' (to lose); commonly used in games, competitions, and sports.

sentences.text: Tim kami menang dalam pertandingan sepak bola.
sentences.en: Our team won the football match.

sentences.text: Dia menang lomba lari di sekolah.
sentences.en: She won the running race at school.

sentences.text: Saya harap kamu menang hari ini.
sentences.en: I hope you win today.

note: 'Menjadi' is the formal form; 'jadi' is the casual spoken form; both mean 'to become/to be'; often confused with 'adalah' which states a fixed identity rather than a change or result

sentences.text: Dia ingin menjadi dokter suatu hari.
sentences.en: She wants to become a doctor someday.

sentences.text: Air itu jadi dingin sekarang.
sentences.en: The water became cold now.

sentences.text: Budi menjadi guru di Bali.
sentences.en: Budi became a teacher in Bali.

note: 'Menjual' is the formal form; 'jual' is used in casual speech and compounds like 'dijual' (for sale) or 'jual-beli' (buying and selling).

sentences.text: Ibu menjual sayur di pasar setiap hari.
sentences.en: Mom sells vegetables at the market every day.

sentences.text: Toko ini jual buah segar dan murah.
sentences.en: This shop sells fresh and cheap fruit.

sentences.text: Dia menjual souvenir kepada para wisatawan.
sentences.en: He sells souvenirs to tourists.

note: 'Menyanyi' is the formal form; 'nyanyi' is the casual spoken shortform — both mean 'to sing'; related words: 'lagu' (song), 'penyanyi' (singer).

sentences.text: Dia suka menyanyi di kamar mandi.
sentences.en: She likes to sing in the bathroom.

sentences.text: Anak-anak nyanyi lagu bersama di kelas.
sentences.en: The children sing a song together in class.

sentences.text: Saya mau nyanyi di pesta besok.
sentences.en: I want to sing at the party tomorrow.

note: Use 'menyanyikan' (or informal 'nyanyikan') when singing a specific song for someone; contrast with 'bernyanyi', which means to sing in general without a specific object.

sentences.text: Dia menyanyikan lagu untuk ibunya.
sentences.en: She sings a song for her mother.

sentences.text: Tolong nyanyikan lagu itu sekali lagi.
sentences.en: Please sing that song one more time.

sentences.text: Anak itu menyanyikan lagu kebangsaan.
sentences.en: That child sings the national anthem.

english: to be good at (doing something), clever, intelligent, smart
note: 'Pandai' means clever or skilled at something; similar to 'pintar' (both common), often used with 'bermain', 'memasak', etc.; neutral, everyday register.

sentences.text: Dia pandai bermain gitar.
sentences.en: She is good at playing guitar.

sentences.text: Anak itu sangat pandai di sekolah.
sentences.en: That child is very clever at school.

sentences.text: Saya ingin pandai berbicara bahasa Indonesia.
sentences.en: I want to be good at speaking Indonesian.

english: once, ever, at some time in the past
note: "Pernah" expresses past experience (have ever done something); often confused with "sudah" (already done); commonly used with "tidak pernah" (never).

sentences.text: Saya pernah makan nasi goreng di Bali.
sentences.en: I once ate fried rice in Bali.

sentences.text: Dia tidak pernah pergi ke pantai.
sentences.en: She has never gone to the beach.

sentences.text: Kamu pernah belajar bahasa Indonesia?
sentences.en: Have you ever studied Indonesian?

note: 'Pintar' means clever or smart and is used for people and animals; often confused with 'pandai', which is a close synonym, but 'pintar' is more common in everyday speech.

sentences.text: Ani sangat pintar di kelas matematika.
sentences.en: Ani is very smart in math class.

sentences.text: Anjing itu pintar dan suka bermain.
sentences.en: That dog is clever and likes to play.

sentences.text: Saya ingin pintar seperti kakak saya.
sentences.en: I want to be smart like my older sibling.

english: absolutely, at all, completely, totally (in negative expressions)
note: Used in negative sentences with 'tidak/tak/bukan' to intensify negation (e.g., 'tidak sama sekali' = 'not at all'); avoid using it in positive statements.

sentences.text: Saya tidak lapar sama sekali hari ini.
sentences.en: I am not hungry at all today.

sentences.text: Dia tidak mengerti sama sekali.
sentences.en: He does not understand at all.

sentences.text: Saya tidak tahu sama sekali tentang itu.
sentences.en: I know absolutely nothing about that.

english: not very..., not especially, not particularly...
note: "Tidak begitu" softens a negative, meaning "not very" or "not that much"; it is more polite than a flat "tidak" (no/not), and beginners often confuse it with "tidak terlalu" which is nearly synonymous.

sentences.text: Saya tidak begitu suka kopi.
sentences.en: I don't really like coffee.

sentences.text: Cuaca hari ini tidak begitu panas.
sentences.en: The weather today is not very hot.

sentences.text: Dia tidak begitu lapar sekarang.
sentences.en: She is not particularly hungry right now.

note: Use 'yang + adjective' after a noun to mean 'the [adjective] one'; very common in everyday speech, e.g. 'yang besar' = 'the big one'.

sentences.text: Saya mau yang merah, bukan yang biru.
sentences.en: I want the red one, not the blue one.

sentences.text: Tolong ambilkan baju yang bersih.
sentences.en: Please get the clean clothes.

sentences.text: Mana tas yang besar?
sentences.en: Which one is the big bag?

note: "Yang lain" means "the other one" or "the others"; often confused with "lainnya" which is slightly more formal; commonly used in everyday choices and comparisons.

sentences.text: Saya mau yang lain, bukan ini.
sentences.en: I want the other one, not this one.

sentences.text: Di mana yang lain pergi?
sentences.en: Where did the others go?

sentences.text: Coba baju yang lain saja.
sentences.en: Just try the other shirt.

english: to use something, to wear something
note: 'Pakai' is informal/everyday; 'memakai' is the formal me- verb form; both mean to use or wear something — often confused with 'mengenakan' which is more formal for wearing clothes.

sentences.text: Dia memakai baju merah hari ini.
sentences.en: She is wearing a red shirt today.

sentences.text: Saya pakai sepeda ke pasar.
sentences.en: I use a bicycle to go to the market.

sentences.text: Anak itu memakai sandal baru.
sentences.en: That child is wearing new sandals.

english: to keep (as a pet, domestic animal or farm animal)
note: "Memelihara" is the formal/full form; "pelihara" appears in compounds like "hewan peliharaan" (pet animal); not to be confused with "merawat" (to care for/nurse).

sentences.text: Saya memelihara kucing di rumah.
sentences.en: I keep a cat at home.

sentences.text: Kakak saya memelihara ayam di kebun.
sentences.en: My older sibling keeps chickens in the yard.

sentences.text: Apakah kamu memelihara ikan di sini?
sentences.en: Do you keep fish here?

english: to teach (someone / students / pupils / a subject), to do teaching
note: "Mengajar" means to teach others (students/pupils); don't confuse with "belajar" (to learn/study) — they are opposites; related: "guru" (teacher), "pelajaran" (lesson).

sentences.text: Bu Sari mengajar matematika di sekolah.
sentences.en: Mrs. Sari teaches mathematics at school.

sentences.text: Ayah saya mengajar anak-anak di sini.
sentences.en: My father teaches children here.

sentences.text: Dia mengajar bahasa Inggris setiap hari.
sentences.en: She teaches English every day.

english: to help someone (especially someone in difficulty)
note: "Tolong" is the casual/polite request form ("please help" or just "please"), while "menolong" is the full verb "to help someone"; both are very common and interchangeable in everyday speech.

sentences.text: Dia menolong nenek membawa tas berat.
sentences.en: He helps the grandmother carry a heavy bag.

sentences.text: Tolong, saya tidak bisa membuka pintu ini.
sentences.en: Please help, I can't open this door.

sentences.text: Saya mau menolong teman saya.
sentences.en: I want to help my friend.

english: to wait, to wait for (someone / something), to await
note: "Menunggu" is the formal/written form; "tunggu" is used in casual speech and commands (e.g., "Tunggu sebentar!" = "Wait a moment!"); commonly paired with objects like orang (person) or bis (bus).

sentences.text: Saya menunggu bis di halte.
sentences.en: I am waiting for the bus at the stop.

sentences.text: Dia menunggu teman di kafe.
sentences.en: She is waiting for a friend at the café.

sentences.text: Tunggu saya di sini, ya!
sentences.en: Wait for me here, okay!

note: 'Minta tolong' is a polite, everyday phrase used to ask someone for help; very common in casual and formal speech; related to 'tolong' alone which can mean 'please help' or 'please'.

sentences.text: Saya minta tolong kepada ibu saya.
sentences.en: I ask for help from my mother.

sentences.text: Dia minta tolong membuka pintu itu.
sentences.en: He asks for help opening that door.

sentences.text: Kami minta tolong ke tetangga kami.
sentences.en: We ask for help from our neighbor.

note: 'Sejarah' means history as a subject or concept; used in school contexts (mata pelajaran sejarah = history subject); not to be confused with 'cerita' (story).

sentences.text: Saya suka belajar sejarah di sekolah.
sentences.en: I like studying history at school.

sentences.text: Bali punya sejarah yang sangat menarik.
sentences.en: Bali has a very interesting history.

sentences.text: Guru sejarah saya sangat baik.
sentences.en: My history teacher is very kind.

note: 'Selalu' means 'always' and is placed before the verb; not to be confused with 'sering' (often) or 'biasanya' (usually).

sentences.text: Saya selalu makan nasi setiap hari.
sentences.en: I always eat rice every day.

sentences.text: Dia selalu pergi ke pantai pagi-pagi.
sentences.en: She always goes to the beach early in the morning.

sentences.text: Kami selalu minum kopi di warung.
sentences.en: We always drink coffee at the small café.

note: 'Selama' means 'for' a duration of time (e.g. selama dua jam = for two hours); don't confuse with 'untuk' (for a purpose/recipient).

sentences.text: Saya belajar bahasa Indonesia selama dua jam.
sentences.en: I study Indonesian for two hours.

sentences.text: Dia tinggal di Bali selama satu minggu.
sentences.en: She stays in Bali for one week.

sentences.text: Kami berenang selama satu jam.
sentences.en: We swim for one hour.

english: alone, on your own (i.e. without a companion)
note: 'Sendirian' means alone/by oneself (no companion); don't confuse with 'saja' (just/only) or 'sendiri' (self/own), though 'sendiri' is closely related and sometimes interchangeable.

sentences.text: Dia makan malam sendirian di rumah.
sentences.en: She eats dinner alone at home.

sentences.text: Saya pergi ke pantai sendirian hari ini.
sentences.en: I went to the beach alone today.

sentences.text: Anak itu bermain sendirian di taman.
sentences.en: That child is playing alone in the park.

note: 'Sudah cukup' is neutral/everyday speech meaning 'that's enough' or 'that will do'; 'sudah' alone means 'already' and 'cukup' alone means 'enough/sufficient'.

sentences.text: Terima kasih, sudah cukup nasinya.
sentences.en: Thank you, that's enough rice.

sentences.text: Uang ini sudah cukup untuk makan.
sentences.en: This money is enough for eating.

sentences.text: Sudah cukup, aku kenyang sekarang.
sentences.en: That's enough, I'm full now.

note: "Tidak pernah" means "never" and is the opposite of "selalu" (always); use "tidak pernah" before a verb, and do not confuse it with "belum pernah" (have never yet done something).

sentences.text: Saya tidak pernah makan durian.
sentences.en: I never eat durian.

sentences.text: Dia tidak pernah datang terlambat.
sentences.en: He never comes late.

sentences.text: Kami tidak pernah pergi ke pantai.
sentences.en: We never go to the beach.

note: 'Waktu' means 'time' in general; also used as 'when' in formal writing; related words: 'jam' (clock/hour), 'hari' (day)

sentences.text: Saya tidak punya waktu sekarang.
sentences.en: I don't have time right now.

sentences.text: Waktu makan siang sudah tiba.
sentences.en: Lunchtime has arrived.

sentences.text: Berapa waktu yang kamu butuhkan?
sentences.en: How much time do you need?

english: finally, in the end, eventually, lastly
note: "Akhirnya" is informal/neutral and very common in everyday speech; often placed at the start of a sentence to show relief or conclusion; related words include "pada akhirnya" (in the end) and "terakhir" (last/final).

sentences.text: Akhirnya kita sampai di pantai!
sentences.en: Finally, we arrived at the beach!

sentences.text: Dia akhirnya makan siang hari ini.
sentences.en: He finally ate lunch today.

sentences.text: Akhirnya hujan berhenti sore ini.
sentences.en: Finally, the rain stopped this afternoon.

note: 'Berapa lama' asks about duration of time; don't confuse with 'berapa' alone (how much/many) or 'sudah berapa lama' (how long have you).

sentences.text: Berapa lama perjalanan ke pantai ini?
sentences.en: How long is the trip to this beach?

sentences.text: Berapa lama kamu tinggal di Bali?
sentences.en: How long are you staying in Bali?

sentences.text: Berapa lama kelas bahasa Indonesia ini?
sentences.en: How long is this Indonesian class?

note: 'Detektif' is a loanword from English/Dutch, used in everyday speech and media; often seen in detective shows and stories; related words: 'polisi' (police), 'penyelidik' (investigator).

sentences.text: Dia adalah seorang detektif yang pintar.
sentences.en: He is a smart detective.

sentences.text: Detektif itu mencari jejak pencuri.
sentences.en: The detective is looking for the thief's trail.

sentences.text: Anak itu ingin menjadi detektif.
sentences.en: That child wants to become a detective.

note: "Di antaranya" means "among them" or "including"; used to introduce examples from a group; don't confuse with "di antara" (between two things).

sentences.text: Ada banyak buah di sini, di antaranya mangga.
sentences.en: There are many fruits here, including mango.

sentences.text: Kami punya teman baru, di antaranya Made.
sentences.en: We have new friends, among them Made.

sentences.text: Banyak wisatawan datang, di antaranya dari Jepang.
sentences.en: Many tourists came, including some from Japan.

note: 'Kaviar' is a loanword from English/Dutch; it is a formal/luxury food term, rarely used in everyday speech but understood in restaurants and stores.

sentences.text: Kaviar adalah makanan mewah dari ikan.
sentences.en: Caviar is a luxury food from fish.

sentences.text: Restoran itu menjual kaviar yang mahal.
sentences.en: That restaurant sells expensive caviar.

note: "Lobi" is a loanword from English used in both hotel/building contexts and political/informal lobbying; commonly heard in everyday speech.

sentences.text: Kami bertemu di lobi hotel.
sentences.en: We meet in the hotel lobby.

sentences.text: Kursi di lobi sangat nyaman.
sentences.en: The chairs in the lobby are very comfortable.

sentences.text: Tunggu saya di lobi, ya.
sentences.en: Wait for me in the lobby, okay.

note: 'Masakan' refers to cooked food, cooking, or cuisine; often confused with 'memasak' (the verb 'to cook'); related: 'masak' (cooked/to cook).

sentences.text: Masakan ibu sangat enak dan lezat.
sentences.en: Mom's cooking is very tasty and delicious.

sentences.text: Saya suka masakan Indonesia sekali.
sentences.en: I really like Indonesian cuisine.

sentences.text: Masakan ini pedas tapi enak.
sentences.en: This dish is spicy but delicious.

note: 'Mawar' means rose; commonly used in flower shops and gifts; related words: 'bunga' (flower), 'merah' (red), 'taman' (garden).

sentences.text: Saya membeli bunga mawar untuk ibu.
sentences.en: I buy a rose for my mother.

sentences.text: Mawar merah itu sangat indah.
sentences.en: That red rose is very beautiful.

sentences.text: Ada banyak mawar di taman ini.
sentences.en: There are many roses in this garden.

note: 'Bayar' is the base form; 'membayar' is the formal/written form — both mean 'to pay'; commonly used at shops, restaurants, and markets.

sentences.text: Saya membayar kopi di warung.
sentences.en: I pay for coffee at the small shop.

sentences.text: Dia bayar tiket masuk pantai.
sentences.en: He pays for the beach entrance ticket.

sentences.text: Kami membayar makan malam bersama.
sentences.en: We pay for dinner together.

note: "Memilih" is the formal/full form; "pilih" is the base root used in commands or casual speech (e.g., "Pilih satu!"); commonly paired with options using "atau" (or).

sentences.text: Saya memilih nasi goreng untuk makan siang.
sentences.en: I choose fried rice for lunch.

sentences.text: Dia memilih baju biru di toko.
sentences.en: She chooses a blue shirt at the store.

sentences.text: Tolong pilih satu oleh-oleh dari Bali.
sentences.en: Please choose one souvenir from Bali.

english: to kiss someone, to smell, to sniff something
note: 'Mencium' covers both kissing and smelling/sniffing; context makes the meaning clear. 'Cium' is the base form used in casual speech.

sentences.text: Ibu mencium pipi adik sebelum tidur.
sentences.en: Mom kisses the younger sibling's cheek before sleeping.

sentences.text: Saya mencium bau bunga di taman.
sentences.en: I smell the flower's scent in the garden.

sentences.text: Anjing itu mencium tanah di halaman.
sentences.en: The dog sniffs the ground in the yard.

note: 'Mewah' means luxurious or fancy; often used for hotels, cars, and food; related word: 'kemewahan' (luxury/noun).

sentences.text: Hotel ini sangat mewah dan indah.
sentences.en: This hotel is very luxurious and beautiful.

sentences.text: Mobil itu terlihat mewah sekali.
sentences.en: That car looks very luxurious.

sentences.text: Mereka makan di restoran mewah.
sentences.en: They eat at a fancy restaurant.

note: "Oleh" means "by" showing who did/made/wrote something; often confused with "untuk" (for) or "dari" (from); very common in passive sentences.

sentences.text: Buku ini ditulis oleh guru saya.
sentences.en: This book was written by my teacher.

sentences.text: Kue ini dibuat oleh ibu.
sentences.en: This cake was made by mom.

sentences.text: Lagu itu dinyanyikan oleh anak-anak.
sentences.en: That song was sung by the children.

note: "Pada waktu" means 'at the time when / when'; slightly more formal than "ketika", common in written and spoken Indonesian.

sentences.text: Pada waktu hujan, saya di rumah.
sentences.en: At the time when it rains, I am at home.

sentences.text: Dia makan pada waktu siang.
sentences.en: She eats at midday.

sentences.text: Pada waktu pagi, pasar sangat ramai.
sentences.en: In the morning, the market is very busy.

note: "Pipi" means cheeks (on the face); commonly used in everyday speech; related words include "wajah" (face) and "bibir" (lips).

sentences.text: Pipi adik sangat merah dan lucu.
sentences.en: My younger sibling's cheeks are very red and cute.

sentences.text: Ibu mencium pipi saya setiap pagi.
sentences.en: Mom kisses my cheeks every morning.

sentences.text: Pipi bayi itu sangat halus.
sentences.en: That baby's cheeks are very smooth.

english: while (one person performing two actions at the same time)
note: "Sambil" means one person does two actions simultaneously; don't confuse with "sementara" (while/meanwhile, often two different subjects).

sentences.text: Dia makan sambil menonton televisi.
sentences.en: He/She eats while watching television.

sentences.text: Saya berjalan sambil minum kopi.
sentences.en: I walk while drinking coffee.

sentences.text: Anak itu bernyanyi sambil bermain.
sentences.en: The child sings while playing.

note: 'Sampanye' is a borrowed word from French/English; used in formal or celebratory contexts, often at parties or restaurants; sometimes called 'anggur bersoda' informally.

sentences.text: Kami minum sampanye di pesta itu.
sentences.en: We drank champagne at that party.

sentences.text: Tolong beli sampanye untuk malam ini.
sentences.en: Please buy champagne for tonight.

sentences.text: Sampanye ini sangat enak dan mahal.
sentences.en: This champagne is very delicious and expensive.

english: happy, enjoying yourself, to like something, to like doing something
note: 'Senang' covers happiness, enjoyment, and liking something; beginners often confuse it with 'suka' (to like/prefer), but both are common and nearly interchangeable in casual speech.

sentences.text: Saya senang belajar bahasa Indonesia.
sentences.en: I enjoy learning Indonesian.

sentences.text: Dia senang makan nasi goreng setiap hari.
sentences.en: She likes eating fried rice every day.

sentences.text: Kami senang bermain di pantai.
sentences.en: We are happy playing at the beach.

note: 'Swasta' describes private (non-government) institutions like schools or companies; opposite is 'negeri' (state/public); common in phrases like 'sekolah swasta' and 'perusahaan swasta'.

sentences.text: Dia bekerja di perusahaan swasta di Bali.
sentences.en: He works at a private company in Bali.

sentences.text: Sekolah swasta itu mahal sekali.
sentences.en: That private school is very expensive.

sentences.text: Rumah sakit swasta ada di sini.
sentences.en: There is a private hospital here.

note: 'Wanita' is a polite, formal word for woman; the casual everyday alternative is 'perempuan', while 'ibu' is used respectfully for older women.

sentences.text: Wanita itu membeli buah di pasar.
sentences.en: That woman is buying fruit at the market.

sentences.text: Dia adalah wanita yang sangat baik.
sentences.en: She is a very kind woman.

sentences.text: Satu wanita duduk di kafe itu.
sentences.en: A woman is sitting at that café.

note: 'Allah' is the Arabic-origin word for God used in Islam; Indonesian Muslims use it widely, while Christians may say 'Tuhan' instead.

sentences.text: Allah Maha Besar dan Maha Kuasa.
sentences.en: God is great and all-powerful.

sentences.text: Dia selalu berdoa kepada Allah setiap hari.
sentences.en: He always prays to God every day.

sentences.text: Allah memberikan rezeki kepada kita semua.
sentences.en: God gives blessings to all of us.

note: 'Allahu Akbar' is an Arabic phrase used widely in Indonesia (a Muslim-majority country) as an expression of awe, gratitude, or during prayer; often heard during the call to prayer (adzan).

sentences.text: Dia berkata 'Allahu Akbar' saat melihat pemandangan.
sentences.en: He said 'Allahu Akbar' when he saw the scenery.

sentences.text: Muazin mengucapkan Allahu Akbar dengan suara keras.
sentences.en: The muezzin said Allahu Akbar in a loud voice.

sentences.text: Kami bersama mengucapkan Allahu Akbar saat salat.
sentences.en: We said Allahu Akbar together during prayer.

english: The Koran (the holy book of Islam)
note: "Al-Qur'an" is the standard Indonesian spelling for the Islamic holy book; also written "Alquran"; treated with great respect in daily speech.

sentences.text: Dia membaca Al-Qur'an setiap pagi.
sentences.en: He/She reads the Koran every morning.

sentences.text: Al-Qur'an ada di atas meja.
sentences.en: The Koran is on the table.

sentences.text: Ibu mengajar anak membaca Al-Qur'an.
sentences.en: Mother teaches the child to read the Koran.

english: a verse, a stanza (from a poem or from holy scripture)
note: "Ayat" is used in formal/religious contexts for a verse of scripture (e.g., Quran, Bible) or a stanza of a poem; closely related to 'surah' (a chapter of the Quran).

sentences.text: Dia membaca ayat dari Al-Quran.
sentences.en: He reads a verse from the Quran.

sentences.text: Guru mengajarkan ayat pendek kepada kami.
sentences.en: The teacher taught us a short verse.

sentences.text: Saya hafal satu ayat hari ini.
sentences.en: I memorized one verse today.

note: "Barang" is a neutral everyday word for a physical item or goods; often used in markets and shops; related: "barang-barang" means belongings/stuff.

sentences.text: Saya membeli barang di pasar.
sentences.en: I buy things at the market.

sentences.text: Barang ini sangat murah.
sentences.en: This item is very cheap.

sentences.text: Di mana barang saya?
sentences.en: Where is my thing/item?

note: 'Batik' refers to traditional Indonesian fabric with wax-resist dyeing patterns; used as both noun and adjective (e.g., baju batik = batik shirt); a point of national pride in Indonesia.

sentences.text: Saya membeli baju batik di pasar.
sentences.en: I buy a batik shirt at the market.

sentences.text: Batik Indonesia sangat indah dan terkenal.
sentences.en: Indonesian batik is very beautiful and famous.

sentences.text: Ibu saya suka memakai batik.
sentences.en: My mother likes to wear batik.

english: to be a follower of such-and-such a religion
note: "Beragama" combines "ber-" (prefix meaning 'to have/practice') + "agama" (religion); used to state someone's religious affiliation, common in formal forms and introductions; related: "agama" (religion), "beragama Islam" (to be Muslim).

sentences.text: Saya beragama Islam sejak kecil.
sentences.en: I have been Muslim since childhood.

sentences.text: Dia beragama Hindu dan rajin bersembahyang.
sentences.en: She is Hindu and diligently prays.

sentences.text: Semua orang di sini beragama Kristen.
sentences.en: Everyone here is Christian.

english: to break your fast, to have a meal in the evening after a day of fasting
note: Used specifically during Ramadan; 'berbuka puasa' is often shortened to 'buka puasa' in casual speech.

sentences.text: Kami berbuka puasa bersama keluarga di rumah.
sentences.en: We break our fast together with family at home.

sentences.text: Dia berbuka puasa dengan kurma dan air.
sentences.en: He breaks his fast with dates and water.

english: to assemble, to gather, to come together
note: 'Berkumpul' is a common everyday verb meaning to gather or come together as a group; related to 'kumpul' (gather) and often used for family or community events.

sentences.text: Keluarga kami berkumpul di rumah setiap Minggu.
sentences.en: Our family gathers at home every Sunday.

sentences.text: Teman-teman berkumpul di pantai sore ini.
sentences.en: Friends gather at the beach this afternoon.

sentences.text: Semua siswa berkumpul di halaman sekolah.
sentences.en: All students gather in the school yard.

english: to fast, to abstain from food and drink
note: "Berpuasa" is a formal/standard verb for fasting, commonly used in religious contexts (especially Ramadan); related words: "puasa" (the noun/fast), "sahur" (pre-dawn meal), "berbuka" (to break the fast).

sentences.text: Saya berpuasa selama satu bulan penuh.
sentences.en: I fast for one full month.

sentences.text: Dia berpuasa hari ini karena Ramadan.
sentences.en: She is fasting today because of Ramadan.

sentences.text: Kami berpuasa bersama keluarga di rumah.
sentences.en: We fast together with family at home.

english: to greet each other (usually by shaking hands)
note: "Bersalaman" is a polite, everyday word for greeting by shaking hands; common in formal and social settings; related to "salam" (greeting/salutation).

sentences.text: Mereka bersalaman sebelum rapat dimulai.
sentences.en: They greet each other before the meeting starts.

sentences.text: Anak itu bersalaman dengan gurunya.
sentences.en: The child greets their teacher with a handshake.

sentences.text: Kami bersalaman saat bertemu di pasar.
sentences.en: We greet each other when we meet at the market.

note: 'Bersyukur' means to be grateful or give thanks to God; more spiritual than 'terima kasih'; often used in daily reflections.

sentences.text: Saya bersyukur atas kesehatan saya hari ini.
sentences.en: I am grateful to God for my health today.

sentences.text: Kita harus bersyukur setiap hari.
sentences.en: We must give thanks to God every day.

sentences.text: Dia bersyukur karena keluarganya sehat.
sentences.en: She is thankful to God because her family is healthy.

english: the next day, the following day
note: 'Besoknya' means 'the next day/the following day' (referring back to a previously mentioned day); more specific than 'besok' (tomorrow); often used in storytelling.

sentences.text: Kami pergi ke pantai besoknya.
sentences.en: We went to the beach the next day.

sentences.text: Besoknya, dia makan nasi goreng lagi.
sentences.en: The next day, he ate fried rice again.

sentences.text: Toko itu buka besoknya pagi.
sentences.en: The shop opened the following day in the morning.

note: "Bulan puasa" informally refers to Ramadan; used in everyday speech alongside the formal term "Ramadan", often associated with fasting, night prayers, and special foods.

sentences.text: Sekarang kita sedang dalam bulan puasa.
sentences.en: Right now we are in the fasting month.

sentences.text: Bulan puasa, banyak orang tidak makan siang.
sentences.en: During the fasting month, many people don't eat lunch.

sentences.text: Saya suka makanan di bulan puasa.
sentences.en: I like the food during the fasting month.

note: 'Di mana-mana' means 'everywhere'; note the reduplication pattern common in Indonesian; related: 'di mana' (where/in which place).

sentences.text: Turis ada di mana-mana di Bali.
sentences.en: Tourists are everywhere in Bali.

sentences.text: Saya lihat bunga di mana-mana.
sentences.en: I see flowers everywhere.

sentences.text: Sampah ada di mana-mana di pantai.
sentences.en: There is trash everywhere on the beach.

english: a prayer (especially a personal, meditative prayer)
note: 'Doa' refers to a personal, heartfelt prayer or blessing; distinct from 'sembahyang' (ritual worship/prayer service); often used in phrases like 'terima kasih atas doa kalian' (thanks for your prayers).

sentences.text: Ibu selalu baca doa sebelum makan.
sentences.en: Mom always says a prayer before eating.

sentences.text: Saya kirim doa untuk nenek saya.
sentences.en: I send a prayer for my grandmother.

sentences.text: Terima kasih atas doa kamu.
sentences.en: Thank you for your prayer.

note: 'Gelap' means dark or dimly lit; often confused with 'hitam' (black color); related: 'kegelapan' (darkness), 'malam gelap' (dark night).

sentences.text: Kamar ini sangat gelap malam ini.
sentences.en: This room is very dark tonight.

sentences.text: Tolong nyalakan lampu, di sini gelap.
sentences.en: Please turn on the light, it is dark here.

sentences.text: Saya takut berjalan di jalan gelap.
sentences.en: I am afraid to walk on a dark street.

english: a feast day, a big religious holiday
note: 'Hari raya' refers to major religious holidays (e.g. Eid, Nyepi); often used with 'Idul Fitri' or alone; more formal than just 'hari libur' (day off).

sentences.text: Besok adalah hari raya Idul Fitri.
sentences.en: Tomorrow is the Eid al-Fitr holiday.

sentences.text: Kami makan bersama saat hari raya.
sentences.en: We eat together during the feast day.

sentences.text: Ibu membeli baju baru untuk hari raya.
sentences.en: Mom bought new clothes for the holiday.

note: 'Haus' means thirsty; not to be confused with 'lapar' (hungry); common in everyday speech.

sentences.text: Saya haus dan ingin minum air.
sentences.en: I am thirsty and want to drink water.

sentences.text: Dia haus setelah bermain di pantai.
sentences.en: She is thirsty after playing at the beach.

sentences.text: Anak itu haus karena cuaca panas.
sentences.en: That child is thirsty because of the hot weather.

english: the festival of Ied, the (usually two) days of celebrations at the end of the Muslim fasting month
note: "Idul Fitri" is the formal/standard term for Eid al-Fitr; colloquially also called "Lebaran" in everyday Indonesian speech; often paired with "Hari Raya" as "Hari Raya Idul Fitri".

sentences.text: Keluarga kami merayakan Idul Fitri bersama.
sentences.en: Our family celebrates Eid al-Fitr together.

sentences.text: Idul Fitri adalah hari libur nasional.
sentences.en: Eid al-Fitr is a national holiday.

sentences.text: Kami makan ketupat saat Idul Fitri.
sentences.en: We eat ketupat during Eid al-Fitr.

note: 'Kali' means 'times' (multiplication or frequency); don't confuse with 'kali' meaning 'river/creek' in Javanese — context makes it clear.

sentences.text: Saya sudah makan dua kali hari ini.
sentences.en: I have already eaten two times today.

sentences.text: Dia pergi ke pasar tiga kali seminggu.
sentences.en: She goes to the market three times a week.

english: lumps of rice boiled in packets made from woven leaves (a special food eaten at Idul Fitri)
note: 'Ketupat' is a festive food term closely associated with Idul Fitri (Eid); beginners may confuse it with plain rice ('nasi'), but ketupat is specifically rice cooked inside a woven palm-leaf pouch.

sentences.text: Ibu membuat ketupat untuk Idul Fitri.
sentences.en: Mom makes ketupat for Idul Fitri.

sentences.text: Saya suka makan ketupat dengan opor ayam.
sentences.en: I like eating ketupat with chicken opor.

sentences.text: Ketupat ini enak sekali.
sentences.en: This ketupat is very delicious.

note: A fixed phrase used in formal or heartfelt contexts, especially greetings like Eid ('Mohon maaf lahir dan batin'); means both outer actions and inner feelings.

sentences.text: Saya minta maaf lahir dan batin.
sentences.en: I sincerely apologize, outwardly and inwardly.

sentences.text: Dia bahagia lahir dan batin.
sentences.en: She is happy outwardly and inwardly.

note: "Lantai" means floor or storey/level of a building; beginners sometimes confuse it with "tanah" (ground/soil) for outdoor surfaces.

sentences.text: Tolong bersihkan lantai di ruang tamu.
sentences.en: Please clean the floor in the living room.

sentences.text: Anak itu duduk di lantai.
sentences.en: The child is sitting on the floor.

sentences.text: Hotel ini punya tiga lantai.
sentences.en: This hotel has three floors.

note: 'Lapar' means hungry; often paired with 'haus' (thirsty); casual everyday register used by all ages.

sentences.text: Saya lapar setelah berolahraga tadi.
sentences.en: I am hungry after exercising just now.

sentences.text: Anak itu lapar dan mau makan.
sentences.en: That child is hungry and wants to eat.

sentences.text: Kamu lapar? Mari kita makan siang.
sentences.en: Are you hungry? Let's have lunch.

english: (the Javanese term for) the period of celebrations at the end of the Muslim fasting month
note: 'Lebaran' is an informal Javanese-origin term widely used across Indonesia as a synonym for 'Idul Fitri'; often confused with the fasting month itself (Ramadan), but Lebaran refers to the celebration after it ends.

sentences.text: Keluarga kami berkumpul saat Lebaran.
sentences.en: Our family gathers during Lebaran.

sentences.text: Ibu membuat kue untuk Lebaran.
sentences.en: Mom makes cookies for Lebaran.

sentences.text: Kami pulang kampung waktu Lebaran.
sentences.en: We go back to our hometown during Lebaran.

english: to be shut/closed (for a holiday etc.), to have time off (from work/school etc.)
note: "Libur" is informal/neutral and used for both people (having a day off) and places (being closed); related words: "liburan" (holiday/vacation), "hari libur" (public holiday).

sentences.text: Hari ini sekolah libur karena hari raya.
sentences.en: Today school is closed because of a holiday.

sentences.text: Saya libur kerja besok.
sentences.en: I have the day off work tomorrow.

sentences.text: Toko itu libur setiap hari Minggu.
sentences.en: That shop is closed every Sunday.

english: to take, to bring, to carry (something somewhere)
note: "Membawa" is the formal/full form; "bawa" is the casual spoken form; often confused with "mengambil" (to fetch/pick up) — membawa implies physically carrying or bringing something along.

sentences.text: Saya membawa tas ke sekolah setiap hari.
sentences.en: I bring my bag to school every day.

sentences.text: Dia membawa air minum untuk kita.
sentences.en: He brings drinking water for us.

sentences.text: Tolong bawa payung, mau hujan.
sentences.en: Please bring an umbrella, it's going to rain.

note: "Memimpin" is the formal verb form; "pimpin" is the base root, often used in commands (e.g., "Pimpin kami!"). Related words: "pemimpin" (leader), "kepemimpinan" (leadership). Common in formal and everyday contexts.

sentences.text: Dia memimpin rapat di kantor hari ini.
sentences.en: He leads the meeting at the office today.

sentences.text: Ibu guru memimpin anak-anak di kelas.
sentences.en: The teacher leads the children in class.

sentences.text: Siapa yang memimpin kelompok kita?
sentences.en: Who is leading our group?

english: to say something, to utter something, to pronounce (a sound)
note: "Mengucapkan" is the formal/full form; "ucapkan" is the imperative or shortened form; commonly used for saying greetings, words, or pronouncing sounds; related to "kata" (word) and "bilang" (to say, informal).

sentences.text: Dia mengucapkan terima kasih kepada guru.
sentences.en: He said thank you to the teacher.

sentences.text: Tolong ucapkan kata itu dengan jelas.
sentences.en: Please pronounce that word clearly.

sentences.text: Kami mengucapkan selamat ulang tahun bersama.
sentences.en: We said happy birthday together.

english: to apologise, to ask for forgiveness
note: 'Minta maaf' is a polite, everyday phrase for apologising; 'maaf' alone is a shorter, equally common form, while 'meminta maaf' is the formal written version.

sentences.text: Saya minta maaf karena datang terlambat.
sentences.en: I apologise for coming late.

sentences.text: Dia minta maaf kepada temannya.
sentences.en: He apologises to his friend.

sentences.text: Kami minta maaf atas kesalahan ini.
sentences.en: We apologise for this mistake.

english: to apologise, to ask for forgiveness
note: "Mohon maaf" is a polite, formal way to apologise, slightly more respectful than "maaf" alone; commonly used in Bali and across Indonesia in shops, temples, and daily greetings.

sentences.text: Mohon maaf, saya terlambat hari ini.
sentences.en: I apologise, I am late today.

sentences.text: Saya mohon maaf karena salah pesan.
sentences.en: I apologise because I ordered the wrong thing.

sentences.text: Mohon maaf, tolong ulangi sekali lagi.
sentences.en: Sorry, please repeat it one more time.

english: to make a visit back to your home village in the countryside, to go upstream
note: 'Mudik' refers specifically to the mass homecoming tradition during Eid (Lebaran), when city workers return to their home villages; commonly associated with crowded travel and family reunions.

sentences.text: Kami mudik ke kampung saat Lebaran.
sentences.en: We go back to the village during Eid.

sentences.text: Bapak mudik naik bus besok pagi.
sentences.en: Dad is going home to the village by bus tomorrow morning.

sentences.text: Banyak orang mudik sebelum Lebaran tiba.
sentences.en: Many people travel back to their villages before Eid arrives.

note: 'Nabi' means a religious prophet, most commonly used in Islamic context (e.g., Nabi Muhammad); it is a respectful, formal-register word used across Indonesia.

sentences.text: Nabi Muhammad adalah utusan Allah.
sentences.en: The Prophet Muhammad is the messenger of God.

sentences.text: Guru bercerita tentang nabi di kelas.
sentences.en: The teacher tells a story about a prophet in class.

sentences.text: Anak-anak belajar kisah para nabi.
sentences.en: The children learn the stories of the prophets.

english: to make the pilgrimage to Mecca
note: "Naik haji" is a formal/religious phrase referring to the Islamic pilgrimage to Mecca; often preceded by "pergi" (go) or "sudah" (already); related: "haji" (the title given after completing it).

sentences.text: Kakek saya ingin naik haji tahun ini.
sentences.en: My grandfather wants to make the pilgrimage to Mecca this year.

sentences.text: Ibu sudah naik haji dua kali.
sentences.en: Mom has already made the pilgrimage to Mecca twice.

sentences.text: Mereka menabung untuk naik haji.
sentences.en: They are saving money to make the pilgrimage to Mecca.

english: a gift/present brought back for family or a friend after a trip somewhere
note: 'Oleh-oleh' is an informal everyday word for souvenirs or gifts brought home from a trip; it is always plural in concept and differs from 'hadiah' (a general gift).

sentences.text: Saya beli oleh-oleh untuk keluarga saya.
sentences.en: I bought souvenirs for my family.

sentences.text: Oleh-oleh dari Bali sangat enak.
sentences.en: The gifts from Bali are very delicious.

sentences.text: Dia membawa oleh-oleh untuk teman-temannya.
sentences.en: She brought back souvenirs for her friends.

note: 'Perabot' means furniture or household items; often used as 'perabot rumah' (house furniture); not to be confused with 'perkakas' which means tools/equipment.

sentences.text: Toko itu menjual perabot rumah yang murah.
sentences.en: That shop sells cheap house furniture.

sentences.text: Kami membeli perabot baru untuk kamar tidur.
sentences.en: We bought new furniture for the bedroom.

sentences.text: Perabot di ruang tamu sangat bagus.
sentences.en: The furniture in the living room is very nice.

note: 'Puasa' refers to fasting, especially the Islamic Ramadan fast; commonly heard in everyday Indonesian life during the fasting month ('bulan puasa').

sentences.text: Hari ini saya puasa dari pagi.
sentences.en: Today I am fasting from the morning.

sentences.text: Bulan puasa sangat spesial di Indonesia.
sentences.en: The fasting month is very special in Indonesia.

sentences.text: Dia tidak makan karena sedang puasa.
sentences.en: She is not eating because she is fasting.

english: a stew of beef chunks cooked until dry in spices and shredded coconut
note: "Rendang" is a famous West Sumatran dish, now popular across Indonesia; often served at special occasions or everyday warungs; related words: 'daging' (meat), 'pedas' (spicy).

sentences.text: Saya makan rendang dengan nasi putih.
sentences.en: I eat rendang with white rice.

sentences.text: Rendang ini sangat enak dan pedas.
sentences.en: This rendang is very delicious and spicy.

sentences.text: Ibu memasak rendang untuk makan malam.
sentences.en: Mom cooks rendang for dinner.

english: a moment, a point in time, a short time, while, during
note: "Saat" means a moment or point in time; commonly used like "when" or "while"; similar to "ketika" but slightly more formal and also used for short durations.

sentences.text: Saat hujan, saya di dalam rumah.
sentences.en: While it was raining, I was inside the house.

sentences.text: Dia datang saat saya makan siang.
sentences.en: He came while I was having lunch.

sentences.text: Tunggu saat ini, tolong.
sentences.en: Please wait a moment.

english: to eat a pre-dawn meal during the fasting month, to eat an early breakfast during the fasting month
note: 'Sahur' refers specifically to the pre-dawn meal eaten before fasting begins during Ramadan; commonly heard in Muslim-majority areas of Indonesia.

sentences.text: Kami sahur bersama keluarga setiap pagi.
sentences.en: We eat the pre-dawn meal together with family every morning.

sentences.text: Ibu memasak nasi untuk sahur.
sentences.en: Mom cooks rice for the pre-dawn meal.

sentences.text: Saya bangun jam empat untuk sahur.
sentences.en: I wake up at four o'clock for the pre-dawn meal.

note: "Sekolah menengah" covers both junior (SMP) and senior (SMA) secondary school; Indonesians often specify "sekolah menengah atas" (SMA) for high school or "sekolah menengah pertama" (SMP) for middle school.

sentences.text: Kakak saya belajar di sekolah menengah.
sentences.en: My older sibling studies at secondary school.

sentences.text: Sekolah menengah itu dekat pasar.
sentences.en: That high school is near the market.

sentences.text: Dia ingin masuk sekolah menengah baru.
sentences.en: He wants to enter a new secondary school.

note: "Setiap" means 'each/every' and is used before nouns or time expressions; beginners sometimes confuse it with "semua" (all), but "setiap" focuses on each individual item or occasion.

sentences.text: Saya minum kopi setiap pagi.
sentences.en: I drink coffee every morning.

sentences.text: Setiap siswa membawa buku ke sekolah.
sentences.en: Every student brings a book to school.

sentences.text: Dia pergi ke pasar setiap hari.
sentences.en: She goes to the market every day.

english: to chant Allahu Akbar (God is Great) in chorus over and over
note: "Takbiran" refers to the communal chanting of 'Allahu Akbar' on the eve of Eid; it is a festive religious activity, not just a single utterance, and is closely associated with Lebaran celebrations in Indonesia.

sentences.text: Kami takbiran bersama di masjid malam ini.
sentences.en: We chant Allahu Akbar together at the mosque tonight.

sentences.text: Anak-anak takbiran keliling kampung dengan gembira.
sentences.en: The children chant Allahu Akbar around the village happily.

note: 'Tempat kerja' means workplace/place of work; 'tempat' means place and 'kerja' means work, so it is a compound noun; related: 'tempat tinggal' (place of residence).

sentences.text: Tempat kerja saya dekat dari rumah.
sentences.en: My workplace is close to home.

sentences.text: Dia pergi ke tempat kerja setiap hari.
sentences.en: He goes to his workplace every day.

sentences.text: Tempat kerja ini sangat bersih.
sentences.en: This workplace is very clean.

note: "Ulama" refers to Islamic scholars with deep religious knowledge; often used as a title of respect in Indonesian Muslim communities; plural form is also "ulama" (not "ulamas").

sentences.text: Ulama itu berbicara tentang agama Islam.
sentences.en: The Islamic scholar speaks about the religion of Islam.

sentences.text: Kami mendengarkan ceramah dari ulama terkenal.
sentences.en: We listen to a lecture from a famous Islamic scholar.

sentences.text: Banyak ulama tinggal di pesantren ini.
sentences.en: Many Islamic scholars live in this Islamic boarding school.
